chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that Satan's *sultan* (authority/power) is conditional, applying only to those who voluntarily follow his whispers and neglect divine commands, rather than being absolute over all believers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of free will (*ikhtiyar*), where spiritual subjugation is a result of human choice rather than predestined coercion. The narration reinforces the concept that believers remain under God's protection unless they align themselves with Satan's path through disobedience.
